result.reasoning:
REFUTED. The op-level arithmetic the reporter shows is real, but it only appears for an input convention the production store does not use, and on the production store the screen measurably does the opposite of what the report claims.

1) What I could reproduce, and what I could not.
Reproduced (ops_ext.py:277, 365): a day with 1 finite minute carrying Ret=+0.01 gives day_zero_ratio = 0.0000; 241 finite minutes of Ret=0 gives 1.0000. So the report's [B] numbers are right as arithmetic. NOT reproduced: the consequence. The value 0.0 needs TWO things at once — (a) the no-trade minutes must be ABSENT (NaN), and (b) every one of the few surviving minutes must carry a non-zero Ret. Both fail on the real store.

2) (a) fails: in the production store a no-trade minute's bar exists and its return is a finite 0, so a thin day reads as near-maximally frozen, not minimally.
The repo's own measurements on the real store say the bars are dense, not sparse:
- /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/docs/new_operators.md:28 defines day_zero_ratio(Ret) as "Ret 在 0 上的点质量(封板 / 停牌 / 无成交的分钟)" — no-trade minutes are counted IN the zero mass, i.e. they are finite zeros.
- /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/alpha_distillation/F101_day_shine_retstd.md:170 (a probe run on the real store): "全天无成交的行 ΔVolume 恒为 0" — a stock-day with no trades at all still has finite Volume=0 on every minute. Bars are present.
- lab/findings.yaml f10x (in_pct): "零 / 近零成交分钟把它炸成极端重尾" — in_pct's denominator is blown up BY zero-volume minutes, which requires them to be finite 0, not NaN.
- lab/findings.yaml:129: "任何「日内收益类统计量 == 0」的格子都是一字板日" — a fully locked day gives day stats of exactly 0, which requires 241 finite zero returns, not NaN.
My [A] script prints what the op then returns for a thin day under each convention (241 nominal minutes, k traded minutes):
  dense bars (no-trade Ret=0): k=1 -> zero_ratio 0.9959; k=2 -> 0.9917; k=40 -> ~0.83 (vs a liquid tick-grid day at ~0.13)
  sparse NaN + non-zero Ret (the report's input): 0.0000
  sparse NaN but the bar's own open->close return (a single-trade bar has open==close): 1.0000
Under the only two conventions consistent with the store, a thin name sits at the TOP of x, exactly where cs_last_high20 throws it out.

3) (b) fails too, even if one assumes sparse bars. For x = cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret),15) to be 0 the stock needs FIFTEEN CONSECUTIVE days with not one minute whose Ret is exactly 0. A-share thin names re-print the same tick constantly. With consecutive trade prices on a 1-tick lattice (50% re-prints), P(no exact-zero return in a day) is 0.26 at k=2 and 0.03 at k=5, so P(x=0 for 15 days running) is 1e-9 / 1e-23. My [B] run includes this case ("sparse_tick_k40"): x = 0.59-0.63, screened 100% of days, held 0%.

4) End-to-end, through the real engine and the real book. [B] builds a synthetic cube with thin names injected under each convention, evaluates the headline expression with CubeEngine, and forms the top-decile book with alphacube.metrics.long_short_weights + partura.books.smoothed(hl=2). Result: the thin names are held 100% of days ONLY in the sparseNaN groups; in the dense groups (k=2 and k=40) and the sparse-barret and sparse-tick groups they are screened out on 100% of days and held 0% — even though their y rank (neg(cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30))) is 0.82-0.99, i.e. y does love them exactly as the report says. The screen catches them anyway.

5) The decisive check: the production-store anatomies already on disk measure the premise directly, and they contradict it. [C] pulls every anatomy signal that carries the cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret),15) screen and compares its book composition with unscreened k_known = cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30):
  成交额(20日):最低20%  held 0.9990 -> 0.6109 mean over 20 screened variants (h_K_ex_both itself: 0.7894), in-segment annual excess -4.14% -> +4.90% (h_K_ex_both: +8.19%)
  成交额(20日):20-40%  held 0.0010 -> 0.2985  (the displaced weight goes to the next quintile up)
  近15日有冻结盘口      held 0.0356 -> 0.0107
The screen displaces 21-39 pp of the THINNEST turnover quintile out of the book and flips that quintile's in-segment excess from negative to positive. That is arithmetically impossible if the thinnest names were sitting at x = 0 and surviving the cut: names removed by a top-20%-of-x cut must have HIGH x, and they are concentrated in the lowest-turnover quintile. So on real data day_zero_ratio(Ret) is high for thin names, the screen fires on them, and "筛子恰好在它要防的那批票上失效" is false. k_known_xfrozen (+18.54%) and h_K_ex_both (+18.10% / holdout +16.78%) are not inflated by this mechanism.

6) Residual, reported as a non-finding: the guard really is only n>0 / n>1, so IF the store ever switched to sparse minute bars (a vendor change, or a partial-day halt that truncates the row), a day with very few finite minutes would read 0.0. Today that costs nothing — with 241 finite minutes per tradable stock-day, a "n >= 30" guard is a no-op. The op also matches its own docstring ("share of the day's FINITE minutes with x == 0"), so there is no definition/implementation mismatch to fix.

result.corrected_fix:
Not needed today — but if the team wants the guard anyway as insurance against a future sparse-bar store, two of the three suggested changes are wrong and should not be made:

1. "分母换成当天的名义分钟数 T 而不是有限分钟数" — do not. On the current dense store T == n, so it changes nothing; on a suspended day it would turn today's clean NaN into 0/241 = 0.0, i.e. it would make a suspended stock read as the LEAST frozen name in the cross-section. That introduces the exact bug the report is worried about.

2. "n >= 30 或 n >= 0.5*T 否则返回 NaN" — harmless but not free. Today it is a no-op (241 finite minutes per tradable stock-day). On any stock-day that IS truncated (a resumption day, an intraday halt, a listing day), NaN-ing x does not merely exclude the name: cs_last_high20/_lexi require isfinite(x), so the name drops out of the signal entirely that day, silently shrinking the universe and moving the benchmark (long_book's ew is taken over names with both signal and label). If it is added, it must be added with a measurement of how many stock-days it NaN-s and a re-run of the k_known_xfrozen / h_K_ex_both rows, not as a quiet hardening.

3. The documentation half of the suggestion is the only part worth doing: say in docs/new_operators.md that the denominator is the day's FINITE minutes and that this is safe only because the production store carries dense bars (a no-trade minute is a finite Ret = 0). That records the data assumption the op depends on, so a vendor/store change gets caught.

result.reasoning:
The premise is factually true but the consequence is false: the two published numbers are exactly the numbers the production reward sees, and the published labels already describe the sign-flipped books, so no number and no conclusion changes.

1. Premise confirmed, consequence not. s2 really has no sign lock (`sign_locked` key absent in every runs/F1*/sweep_s2.json; seg_hiliq_p sign=-1 in 15/15, seg_new_p -1 in 14/15 — F111 is +1), and s3 locks them all to +1. But the lock added at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/sweep.py:142 is the ONLY sign lock in the repo (grep over partura/ and scripts/). The reward that actually drives the search, /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/steer.py:426, does `for sign in (1.0, -1.0)` and keeps the best "(direction, half-life) BY THE LONG BOOK on train". So the "现在的方向约定" the finding appeals to does not exist in the reward: direction is maximized over, not locked to +1.

2. Reproduced: the published s2 row IS the reward-convention row. s2 and s3 are the same data (splits, expression and v_base/k_known utrain Sharpes bit-identical for all 15 factors), so they are simply the two directions of the same panel. Picking per factor the direction with the higher train long Sharpe (what steer.reward keeps) and then scoring on utrain reproduces the published row digit for digit:
   seg_hiliq_p  d_median +1.01, up 87%, down 7%, both 93%  (= the 3.1 table row; s3-locked row is -3.18/0%/100%)
   seg_new_p    d_median +0.41, up 60%, down 13%, both 27% (= the 3.1 table row; s3-locked row is -4.47/0%/100%)
   The s2 direction beats the locked +1 direction on the train long book in 14/15 factors for both ids. The s3 numbers are the LOSING direction, which the reward would never keep.

3. The label is right, not reversed. I ran the real operator: `cs_first_high40(y,x) = rank(y) + 1[rank(x)>0.6]`, so negating it puts the whole high-turnover 40% below everything else; `-1 * cs_first_high40(X, LIQ)` is per-day order-IDENTICAL to `cs_last_high40(neg(X), LIQ)` (verified exactly), and its top decile is 0% drawn from the high-40% turnover segment (100% for the locked +1 version). That is precisely the published label "把成交额最高四成排到最后" (scripts/guidance_report.py:91) — note sweep.py's own `why` string for the same id says the opposite ("只在成交额最高 40% 里选"), i.e. the report author deliberately relabeled to the measured book. The sign-flipped screen is therefore NOT silently mis-scored here.

4. Conclusion 1 / R2 / U5 are untouched. motif_stats rows are byte-identical between s2 and s3 for seg_lowliq_m (+1.18/87%/7%/93%), seg_lowliq_p, seg_xfrozen_m and scr_xhi_p — their rank IC sign was already +1. The +1.2 / "13 of 15" / "14 of 15" figures quoted in conclusion 1 and in guidance/B01.yaml R2's `why` all come from seg_lowliq_m, so they do not move at all. result.reasoning:
The finding's MECHANICAL description is accurate and I reproduced all of it by tree surgery (not string counting). But its stated consequence — that §3.6/D7 is "测的是删掉整个分母" and therefore "这批数据…不支持『比值形式有害』" — is false. No number is wrong and no conclusion changes. Four independent grounds:

(1) THE DENOMINATOR-PRESERVING TEST EXISTS, IS CITED IN D7, AND IS STRONGER. D7's own `why` at guidance/B01.yaml:111 reads 「删掉 div 73% 明显变好;**div → mul 83% 变好**」 and its `evidence:` lists THREE sources, two of them substitutions: `substitute_pairs."div → mul"` and `substitute_outgoing."div →"`. I reconstructed all 12 `div → mul` rows by tree surgery as `make_node(mul, SAME operands, window)` — 12/12 keep the denominator subtree in full (2–19 nodes). Those rows give d_median +0.88, up 83%, down 8%, i.e. strictly stronger than the ablation row (+0.97/73%/27%). So the batch contains a direct, denominator-preserving a/b-vs-a*b test, it is the operand-dropping-free evidence the finding says is missing, and it points the same way. The ablation row corroborates D7; it is not load-bearing.

(2) THE THREE-WAY FAN-OUT CANNOT BE A DENOMINATOR-SUBTREE EFFECT. div→mul d_med +0.88 (up 83%, down 8%), div→add +0.01 (50/50), div→sub −0.84 (down 58%). All three keep the identical denominator subtree in the identical position; only the combining operator changes. A "these denominator subtrees are harmful" story cannot generate that ordering. The data therefore does discriminate the FORM, which is exactly what D7 claims.

(3) THE SUGGESTED FIX'S PREMISE IS FACTUALLY WRONG. It says 「二元节点用 ab→a 与 ab→b 两条,当前只有前者」. propose.py already emits ab→b as `only_{v}_R` (kind `interaction`, why 「只留 … 的右支」): 25 scored rows across 6 factors, including `only_O_R`/`only_AA_R`/`only_M_R`, the right-branch twins of the very div ablations in question. The ab→a direction is deduped into `abl_` because the ablate block runs before the interaction block and `add()` dedups by expr — which is why `only_*_L` is nearly absent. Both directions already exist; they are filed under two `kind`s.

(4) THE TABLE ALREADY CARRIES THE GUARD, AND THE SOFT-DENOMINATOR READING ALREADY HAS ITS OWN STRONGER RULE. The header's own stated reading rule is 「d ≈ 0 **且 ρ原式 ≈ 1** = 这个节点是乘客」; the div row is d_med +0.97 with rho_orig_median 0.404, failing both halves, so a reader applying the printed rule concludes "not a passenger, this removed a lot of the factor" — correct. result.corrected_fix:
No change to `action` is warranted — but the SUGGESTED fix must not be applied as written, because one half of it would silently disable the rule instead of narrowing it:

1. `unless` in this matcher is a WHOLE-TREE search, not a positional guard. `Rule.hits` (partura/steer.py:223) calls `self.unless.matches(n)` on the full tree, and `Pattern.find` (line 152-155) walks every node unless the pattern carries `root:`. So `unless: add(_, _)` would exempt every expression that contains an `add` ANYWHERE — most of the corpus — turning B3 off. The pattern language has no "inside an `add`" operator; the only way to express it would be to write the positive shape out, e.g. a `root: add(_, {mul|div}(_, {cs_mean|...}(_)))` rule, not an `unless`.

2. Adding `root:` is safe with respect to `operator_weights()` (B3 stays non-generic because its second argument is `{cs_mean|...}(_)`, so line 334's `generic` test keeps it out of the per-operator fallback), but it is also unnecessary: the measured cost of the ban is +0.04 Sharpe.

If the rule is touched at all, the two defensible edits are both cheap and change no number:
 (a) make the `why` state the measured magnitude instead of claiming an exact no-op — e.g. "a day scalar spread across the cross-section is worth +0.04 pure-long Sharpe / +0.2pp even at hl=20 (h_rv_fold_state_weight 2.25/+0.103/+0.065 vs h_rv_fold 2.21/+0.101/+0.065); as a blend weight a fixed constant ties or beats it" — and add `"F109 verdict LF3"` to `evidence` beside `"F101 verdict LF5"`, since LF3 is the controlled constant-weight vs state-weight comparison.
 (b) for completeness only, close the two holes with additional patterns rather than by rewriting this one: the matcher has no commutative matching and brace-head alternation cannot express "either operand", so order-insensitivity needs a sibling rule `{mul|div}({cs_mean|cs_sum|cs_median|cs_stddev_full|cs_state_rank}(_), _)`, and the wrapper escape needs `{mul|div}(_, {inv|neg}({cs_mean|cs_sum|cs_median|cs_stddev_full|cs_state_rank}(_)))`.

    z = torch.zeros(x.shape[:-1] + (1,), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)

    y = _f(y)

    st = _trailing_rank(m, 241)                                  # NaN where the state is undefined
    ok = torch.isfinite(y) & torch.isfinite(st).unsqueeze(-1)    # no state -> no signal
